# Source: README.md

# web-text-mirror

Turn one or more live websites into a **single consolidated Markdown file** — one page
after another, each preceded by a `URL:` header. Built for producing clean, LLM/search/
RAG-ready corpora from wikis, forums, docs sites, and blogs. Includes a Chrome side-panel
extension that saves the current tab (or kicks off a whole-site crawl) through a local
HTTP API.

## Quick start

```bash
# one-off crawl of a site (deps auto-install on first run)
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py https://wiki.example.org/

# custom output, depth-capped, slower
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py https://wiki.example.org/ --out out/mirror.md --max-depth 2 --delay 1.5

# start the local API for the Chrome extension (127.0.0.1:8765)
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py --serve      # or just: python3 scripts/text_mirror.py
                                            # (no args defaults to serve mode)
```

Output lands in `text-mirror/<hostname>.md` by default, with a resumable per-host
`<host>.<destination-key>_state.json` and a `crawl.log` beside it.

## Features

- **BFS crawl** from each seed, same-host scoped (normalized host comparison — case,
  default ports, userinfo).
- **Readable-text extraction** via [trafilatura](https://trafilatura.readthedocs.io/)
  (Markdown; tables, comments, links, images kept; boilerplate stripped).
- **Polite:** robots.txt per host (fail-open on network error, honoring 4xx allow and 5xx disallow), global per-request rate limiter (`--delay` / `--req-per-sec`),
  descriptive UA.
- **Public-only:** skips login/register/account/asset/action URLs.
- **Incremental + resumable:** appends after every page; atomic per-host state file
  lets an interrupted crawl resume.
- **Chrome extension** (`chrome-plugin/`): side panel to save the current tab's
  rendered DOM or start/stop/watch a crawl via `http://localhost:8765`.
- **Hardened local API:** binds 127.0.0.1 only, Origin allowlist (extension +
  loopback), browser-supplied output filenames confined to the output directory,
  single-flight crawl guard.

## Architecture

A single Python process runs the crawler; `--serve` adds a threading HTTP server on
127.0.0.1:8765 that the Chrome side-panel extension calls (`/save`, `/crawl`, `/stop`,
`/list`). Details: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Offline clone and optional integrations

`--clone` writes HTML and assets alongside Markdown. Open the clone's `index.html`;
`_clone-manifest.json` lists written, failed and pending resources. Resource filenames
use fragment-free URL hashes to prevent collisions. Missing resources retain live
absolute links. Clone acquisition is unsharded; `--clone` with `--shard-count > 1`
is rejected because asset discovery cannot safely cross shards.

Text crawls support `--max-pages`, `--shard-index` and `--shard-count`.
`--no-prefer-llms` disables the optional workstation `llms_acquire` fast path.
Cloning always uses HTML acquisition. See [integration details](docs/integrations-and-assumptions.md).
The optional `/crawl_llms_txt` and `/distill` API routes can invoke external models
or semantic indexing. They are not used by the bundled panel and are never run
live by the offline tests.

# Source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# Architecture

## Context

web-text-mirror converts public websites into a single consolidated Markdown file for
LLM/search/RAG ingestion. Actors: an operator running the CLI, and optionally the
bundled Chrome side-panel extension driving the same engine through a local HTTP API.
External integrations: the target websites themselves (HTTP GET), each host's
`robots.txt`, and PyPI (one-time self-bootstrap of trafilatura/lxml).

## Container diagram

```
┌────────────────────────── Operator machine ──────────────────────────┐
│                                                                      │
│  Chrome ──────────────┐            ┌──────── python3 text_mirror.py ─┴──┐
│  ┌─────────────────┐  │  HTTP JSON │  ┌────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ chrome-plugin/  │──┼───────────▶│  │ ThreadingHTTPServer        │    │
│  │ side panel      │  │ 127.0.0.1  │  │ /save /crawl /stop /list   │    │
│  │ (sidepanel.js)  │◀─┼── :8765 ───│  └──────────┬─────────────────┘    │
│  └─────────────────┘  │            │             │ spawns (single-flight)│
│                       │            │  ┌──────────▼─────────────────┐    │
│                       │            │  │ crawl(): BFS queue          │    │
│                       │            │  │  ├ robots.txt gate          │    │
│                       │            │  │  ├ rate limiter (_throttle) │    │
│                       │            │  │  └ ThreadPoolExecutor (10)  │───────▶ target sites
│                       │            │  └──────────┬─────────────────┘    │   (HTTP GET)
│                       │            │             │ appends              │
│                       │            │   text-mirror/<host>.md            │
│                       │            │   <host>.<destination-key>_state.json (atomic)       │
│                       │            │   crawl.log                        │
│                       │            └────────────────────────────────────┘
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Components per container

- **CLI / entrypoint** (`main()`): argparse, log setup, seed loop, serve-mode wait loop.
- **Crawl engine** (`crawl()` → `_crawl_impl()`): BFS queue, batching, depth limit,
  resume-from-state, cancel handling; `fetch_and_extract()` per URL.
- **Extraction**: trafilatura `fetch_url` + `extract` (Markdown, tables/comments/
  links/images, favor_recall) with `lxml` link harvesting (`links_from`).
- **Politeness**: `get_robots()` (timeout, fail-open on network error, 4xx allow and 5xx disallow), `_throttle()` global rate limiter, `SKIP_EXT`/`SKIP_SUBSTR` public-only
  filters, descriptive UA.
- **Persistence**: `append_to_file()` (single Markdown file, `URL:` separators),
  `save_state()`/`load_state()` (atomic per-host JSON: crawled map, discovered set,
  queue).
- **Local API** (`PluginServerHandler`): `/save` (extension-supplied DOM → extract →
  append), `/crawl` (spawn crawl thread), `/stop` (cancel flag), `/list` (saved URLs +
  live stats). Guards: 127.0.0.1 bind, `_origin_ok` allowlist, `client_out_file`
  filename confinement, single-flight via `CRAWL_START_LOCK`/`CRAWL_ACTIVE`.
- **Chrome extension** (`chrome-plugin/`): MV3 side panel; captures
  `document.documentElement.outerHTML` of the active tab via `chrome.scripting`,
  posts to the API, polls `/list` at 1 Hz.

## Runtime views

**CLI crawl:** 1) parse args → 2) acquire single-flight reservation → 3) fetch
robots.txt → 4) load/resume state → 5) pop ≤10 URLs, filter (depth/saved/robots) →
6) throttled parallel fetch+extract → 7) append pages, harvest same-host links →
8) periodic atomic state save → 9) repeat until queue empty/cancelled → 10) final save.

**Extension save:** 1) user clicks Save → 2) side panel grabs rendered DOM →
3) `POST /save {url, html, out_file?}` → 4) origin check → filename confinement →
extract → append → 5) response includes updated saved-URL list.

## Deployment topology

Single machine, no daemon: run ad hoc from a shell. The API server binds
`127.0.0.1:8765` only. Output tree defaults to `./text-mirror/`.

## Architectural decisions (ADRs)

1. **Single-file crawler** — ships verbatim inside a Claude skill; no packaging.
2. **Threads over asyncio** — stdlib `http.server` + `ThreadPoolExecutor` keep the
   file dependency-light; concurrency needs are modest (10 workers).
3. **Fail-open robots on network error** — an unreachable robots.txt must not
   silently zero out a crawl; HTTP 4xx allow and 5xx disallow (stdlib-compatible policy).
4. **Append-only output + atomic state** — partial output stays usable after a
   crash; `os.replace` guarantees the resume file is never truncated JSON.
5. **Global rate limiter** — politeness is enforced per request across all worker
   threads, matching the documented `--delay`/`--req-per-sec` contract.
6. **Local-API hardening as product behavior** — 127.0.0.1 bind, Origin allowlist,
   and output-filename confinement are invariants, not options.

## Constraints and quality attributes

- Politeness: default 1 req/s; robots.txt honored per host.
- Unbounded sites (forums/wikis) can explode — `--max-depth` is the operator's cap.
- Memory: BFS `seen` set and state grow with the URL space; large crawls are
  disk/RAM-linear.
- Public-only by design: no authentication, ever.


## Clone and optional integration runtime views

With `--clone`, HTML acquisition feeds both Markdown extraction and `SiteCloner`.
Cloning bypasses llms acquisition because Markdown alone cannot produce an HTML clone.
Assets are queued once, fetched with bounded bodies/timeouts and paced on all attempts,
then links are finalized against files actually written. URL hashes separate resource
identities from clone metadata. Directory-descriptor writes refuse symlink traversal.
The single-flight reservation remains held through clone finalization.

Text-only shard state exchanges discovered URL depths. HTML clones refuse sharding
until a reliable cross-shard asset-discovery/manifest contract exists. This prevents
silent missing assets and competing manifest replacement.

Optional workstation integrations add subprocesses beyond the core diagram:
`llms_acquire` may fetch a site's own Markdown; `/crawl_llms_txt` invokes a headless
editing agent; `/distill` invokes a semantic distiller then an external docset indexer.
No such tool is installed or started by this repository's maintenance or CI.

Resume filenames include the destination basename and shard count in their identity.
Legacy host-only state is retained and ignored. Renaming output or changing shard count
starts independent state. Keep output and state together; do not mix legacy state into
an unrelated file. See the maintenance runbook before upgrading an existing corpus.

Clone resumption validates a version2 manifest and retains canonical HTML/CSS beneath
`_original/`. Finalization replays canonical sources against cumulative written resources,
preserving the original entry and allowing newly acquired pages to become local links.
Text completion and HTML completion are separate; a later clone fetches saved text pages
without duplicating their Markdown blocks. Legacy clone manifests require a fresh directory.

# Source: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md

# Development

## Prerequisites

- Python ≥ 3.11 (CI runs 3.11 and 3.13; local maintenance also verified on Python 3.15)
- pip; optionally a venv
- Chrome (only for extension work)
- `ruff` for linting (`pip install ruff`)

## First-run setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mithudso/web-text-mirror.git
cd web-text-mirror
python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python3 tests/test_text_mirror.py   # should end with ALL PASS
```

The crawler also self-bootstraps trafilatura/lxml via pip on first run if you skip
the install step (see `ensure_deps()`); `scripts/install.sh` pre-provisions instead.

## Local workflow

```bash
# quick functional run against a small site
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py https://example.org/ --max-depth 1

# serve the extension API
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py --serve
# then: chrome://extensions → Developer mode → Load unpacked → chrome-plugin/
```

No watch mode / live reload — it's a single script; rerun it.

## Tests

```bash
python3 tests/test_text_mirror.py
```

One self-contained harness: unit checks on the pure helpers plus a functional
two-page crawl against a throwaway localhost server. Exit code 0 = pass. For focused regression runs, use `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_regressions.py -k <name> -v` for a regression case.

## Lint / syntax

```bash
ruff check scripts/ tests/
python3 -m py_compile scripts/text_mirror.py
```

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — on every PR and push to main: syntax check, ruff, and
the test harness on Python 3.11 and 3.13.

## Branch and commit conventions

Work on feature branches; PR into `main`. Never commit crawl output (`text-mirror/`,
`crawl.log`, `*_state.json` are gitignored). Short imperative commit subjects.

## Adding a feature (walkthrough)

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` Key conventions (security invariants, single-file rule).
2. Change `scripts/text_mirror.py`; keep new shared state behind a lock.
3. Add checks to `tests/test_text_mirror.py` (localhost only).
4. Update `SKILL.md` + `README.md` + relevant docs if the CLI surface changed.
5. Run the three gates above; open a PR.

## Environment variables

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CRAWL_DELAY` | `1.0` | Seconds between requests (CLI `--delay` overrides) |
| `MAX_DEPTH` | `0` | Depth cap in hops, 0 = unlimited (CLI `--max-depth` overrides) |
| `PYTHON` | `python3` | `scripts/install.sh` only: interpreter to provision |

## Troubleshooting

- **`[bootstrap] ERROR: could not install deps`** — pip can't install into the
  current interpreter; create a venv or run `scripts/install.sh` with `PYTHON=` set.
- **Extension shows "Error communicating with crawler"** — the API isn't running;
  start `python3 scripts/text_mirror.py --serve` (port 8765).
- **Crawl saves 0 pages** — check `crawl.log` for `robots-skip` (site disallows) vs
  `no-content` (fetch/extract failures).
- **`409 busy` from `/crawl`** — another crawl is running; `/stop` it first.


See [Testing](TESTING.md) for all offline gates and [the wiki](wiki/README.md) for the maintained command index.

# Source: docs/COMPONENTS.md

# Components

## Layer: crawler (`scripts/text_mirror.py`)

| Component | Purpose | Inputs → outputs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ensure_deps()` | Self-bootstrap trafilatura/lxml via pip (4 escalating strategies incl. `--user`, `--break-system-packages`) | env → installed modules | Runs at import; exits on total failure |
| `log(msg)` | Timestamped stdout + append to `crawl.log` | str → side effect | `LOG_LOCK`-guarded |
| `_throttle(delay)` | Global per-request rate limiter across worker threads | delay → blocking sleep | Monotonic clock; `_RATE_LOCK` |
| `norm(url)` / `norm_host(netloc)` | URL defrag/strip; netloc normalization (case, userinfo, :80/:443) | str → str | Host comparison basis |
| `wanted(url, host)` | Same-host + scheme + skip-list filter | url, host → bool | `SKIP_EXT`, `SKIP_SUBSTR` |
| `get_robots(host, scheme)` | Fetch+parse robots.txt with timeout; fail-open on network error; 4xx → allow; 5xx → disallow | host → `RobotFileParser` | 30 s timeout |
| `links_from(html, base, host)` | Harvest same-host `<a href>` links | html → [url] | lxml; parse errors logged |
| `get_out_file` / `client_out_file` | Resolve output path; confine browser-supplied names to base dir (basename-only; rejects empty/dot/traversal/null/dir-collision) | → abs path or None | Security boundary |
| `get_state_file` / `load_state` / `save_state` / `_load_queue` | Per-host resume state, schema-tolerant load, atomic write (`os.replace`) | ↔ `<host>.<destination-key>_state.json` | `STATE_LOCK` |
| `_mark_saved` / `_is_saved` / `_saved_snapshot` / `_reset_saved` | O(1) saved-URL set + ordered list for `/list` | ↔ `SAVED_URLS`/`_SAVED_SET` | `MIRROR_LOCK` |
| `append_to_file(path, text, url)` | Append one page block (`URL:` separator) | → output .md | `MIRROR_LOCK` |
| `process_single_url(...)` | `/save` path: extract supplied DOM (or fetch) → append | url/html → bool | Same extract options as crawl |
| `fetch_and_extract(...)` | Worker: throttled fetch → extract → link harvest | url → (url, text, links, raw_html) | No-content: (u,None,None,None) |
| `crawl(...)` → `_crawl_impl(...)` | BFS engine; wrapper guarantees `CRAWL_ACTIVE` reset on any exit | seed → n pages | Single-flight with server |
| `PluginServerHandler` | HTTP API: `/save` `/crawl` `/stop` `/list` + CORS/OPTIONS | JSON ↔ JSON | `_origin_ok` gate; 400/403/409/500 semantics |
| `run_server(delay)` | `ThreadingHTTPServer` on 127.0.0.1:8765 | — | Daemon thread |
| `main()` | argparse, log setup, serve thread, seed loop w/ single-flight interlock | argv → exit | |

## Layer: extension (`chrome-plugin/`)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | MV3; permissions: sidePanel, activeTab, scripting; CORS-based loopback access; no broad host permissions |
| `background.js` | Opens the side panel on toolbar click (3 lines) |
| `sidepanel.html` | Panel UI: crawl checkbox, max-depth, force-refresh, out-file, saved list |
| `sidepanel.js` | Captures tab DOM via `chrome.scripting.executeScript`, POSTs `/save` or `/crawl`, polls `/list` at 1 Hz, toggles Stop button |

## Layer: tooling

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/install.sh` | Optional pre-provisioning of trafilatura (`PYTHON=` override) |
| `tests/test_text_mirror.py` | Self-contained unit + functional harness (see docs/TESTING.md) |

## Dependency graph

`sidepanel.js → localhost:8765 → PluginServerHandler → process_single_url/crawl →
{trafilatura, lxml, urllib} → target sites`. The crawler imports only stdlib +
trafilatura + lxml. The extension has no build deps.


## Offline clone utility (`scripts/site_clone.py`)

`url_to_rel_path(url, host)` maps each fragment-free URL into `_resources/<sha256>.<ext>`.
`page_links` includes HTML links and explicit srcset candidates. `rewrite_css` preserves
import syntax and local fragments. `rewrite_html` serializes UTF-8 and normalizes charset
metadata. `fetch_bytes` returns `(bytes, content_type, effective_url)` with a 32 MiB body cap.
`SiteCloner(root, host, ua, log=..., max_assets=..., delay=...)` accepts pages through
`save_page`, drains assets with `fetch_assets`, and rewrites only available resources in
`write_manifest`. Failed/pending resources stay absolute. `index.html` opens the entry page;
`_clone-manifest.json` records results. Sharded clone construction is rejected.

Example (synthetic HTML, no asset requests):

```python
from scripts.site_clone import SiteCloner
clone = SiteCloner('/tmp/example-clone', 'example.org', 'local-example')
clone.save_page('https://example.org/', '<html><body>Example</body></html>')
clone.fetch_assets()
clone.write_manifest()
```

## Optional host integrations and tooling

`try_llms_acquire` is a guarded fast path; `_crawl_llms_txt_job` owns the optional
agent queue. `run_distill_job` invokes external semantic tools. Their contracts and
risks are [documented separately](integrations-and-assumptions.md); they are mocked
in tests. `scripts/maintain_docs.py` parses source without imports and owns generated
references; `scripts/rotate_workflow_logs.py` archives oversized workflow logs.

# Source: docs/SECURITY.md

# Security

## Trust boundaries and principals

| Boundary | Untrusted side | Trusted side |
|---|---|---|
| Local HTTP API (127.0.0.1:8765) | Anything that can reach loopback: other local processes, and — via the browser — any web page issuing cross-origin requests | The crawler process |
| Fetched web content | Target sites' HTML | lxml/trafilatura parsers |
| Filesystem | Browser-supplied `out_file` values | Output base directory |
| PyPI (bootstrap) | Package index | Local interpreter |

Principals: the operator (full trust), the bundled Chrome extension
(`chrome-extension://` origin — trusted client), everything else on the network
(untrusted).

## Authentication and authorization

The API has no credentials; it relies on three enforced invariants:

1. **Bind 127.0.0.1 only** (`run_server`) — nothing off-machine can connect.
2. **Origin allowlist** (`_origin_ok`) — requests with an `Origin` header are
   rejected unless it is `chrome-extension://`/`moz-extension://` or loopback
   (`localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/`::1`). `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframes) is rejected;
   header-less clients (curl, scripts) are allowed. This filter is defense in depth, not authentication. Local processes are trusted.
3. **Output confinement** (`client_out_file`) — browser-supplied `out_file` is
   reduced to a basename inside the output base dir; empty/dot/traversal/null-byte
   names and collisions with existing directories are rejected.

## Secret management

No credentials are required by the core crawler. `.env` is gitignored defensively; never log or
commit tokens.

## Input validation

- HTTP bodies: JSON parse + required-field checks → 400; non-integer or negative limits rejected; `/save` failures → 500 with logged reason.
- URLs: scheme restricted to http/https and host-matched in `wanted()`; skip lists
  drop auth/asset/action URLs.
- Fetched HTML: parsed by lxml/trafilatura; parse failures are caught and logged.

## STRIDE mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Spoofing (web page posing as extension) | Origin allowlist; extensions' origins are browser-enforced |
| Tampering (state/output corruption) | Atomic state writes (`os.replace`); locks around shared state |
| Repudiation | `crawl.log` records every save/skip/error with timestamps |
| Information disclosure | Server binds loopback; responses expose only crawl metadata |
| DoS (wedging the crawler) | Single-flight guard with guaranteed `CRAWL_ACTIVE` reset; handler exceptions → HTTP errors, not crashes |
| Elevation (arbitrary file write) | `client_out_file` confinement; CLI `--out` is operator-trusted by design |

Residual risk (accepted): any *local* process can drive the API — the API's
capability equals what the same local user could do anyway. SSRF-style fetches of
internal URLs are inherent to a crawler; the Origin gate blocks the browser as a
confused deputy, and header-less local callers are already trusted.

## Bootstrap supply chain

`ensure_deps()` pip-installs unpinned trafilatura/lxml at first import, escalating to
`--break-system-packages`. This is a deliberate usability trade-off for the
skill-packaging use case; `requirements.txt` documents floor versions and
`scripts/install.sh` is the explicit alternative. Pin exact versions if you need
reproducibility.

## Contributor checklist

- [ ] Does the change touch `run_server`, `_origin_ok`, or `client_out_file`? →
      security review + tests.
- [ ] New shared state → which lock guards it?
- [ ] New external input (HTTP field, env var, file) → validated where it enters?
- [ ] Nothing sensitive logged.

## Incident response

Logs: stdout + `crawl.log` next to the output file. Contact: repository owner
(@mithudso) via GitHub security advisory (see `.github/SECURITY.md`).

## Compliance

Crawls public content only; obeys robots.txt (4xx → allow; 5xx → disallow); no compliance or privacy attestation is made. Operators choose the content.


## Maintenance hardening and residual trust

The API rejects non-loopback Host headers to block browser DNS rebinding.
JSON requests require an object with a typed HTTP(S) URL, bounded 8 MiB body and
read timeout. Credentials, whitespace, control characters and dot-only hosts are
rejected. Browser clone directory names are confined beside output. Clone writes
use no-follow directory descriptors and atomic replacement; Markdown append refuses
a symlink basename. URL hashing prevents remote path names from colliding with clone
metadata. Optional model jobs are powerful local capabilities: they can invoke an
editing agent or semantic indexer and must not be exposed outside the operator's
trusted machine. Tests mock them; the repository does not attest to external tool
safety or backend correctness. Clone HTML contains active original scripts; it is
not sanitized static prose.

Existing URL logs can include sensitive path/query data. Avoid such inputs and treat
local logs as operator data. No security response-time SLA is declared; a maintainer
must explicitly adopt one if desired. No license or conduct policy was changed.

# Source: docs/TESTING.md

# Testing

## Commands and layers

Install `python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`; use Python 3.11+ and Node 22+.
No build step exists.

| Command | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `python tests/test_text_mirror.py` | Existing helper assertions and two-page localhost crawl; bounded local fetch adapter isolates the fixture from upstream response suitability thresholds |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_regressions.py -v` | Destination identity, cancellation/resume, refresh, duplicate writes, API validation/status, optional-job cleanup, clone mapping/CSS/HTML/assets/limits/symlinks and tooling |
| `node --test tests/test_sidepanel.js` | Mock DOM/Chrome/fetch; HTTP rejection, capture errors, depth validation, duplicate clicks, safe rendering and background rejection |
| `ruff check scripts/ tests/` | Python lint |
| `python -m compileall -q scripts tests` | Python syntax across maintained components |
| `bash -n scripts/install.sh` | Installer syntax |
| `node --check chrome-plugin/background.js` and `node --check chrome-plugin/sidepanel.js` | Extension JavaScript syntax |
| `python scripts/maintain_docs.py --check` | Static reference path/content drift |

Run a single regression with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_regressions.py -k output_state -v`.
GitHub CI runs all gates on Python 3.11 and 3.13, with Node 22. A failure blocks delivery.

## Fixture and assertion rules

Tests preblock the optional host module before importing the crawler. Optional
subprocess/model/indexing integrations are mocked. Network fixtures bind only a
throwaway loopback port and use synthetic HTML; no public site, private corpus,
API token, model or semantic service participates. Preinstall dependencies so import
cannot invoke the fallback pip bootstrap.

Assert observable results: output banners, saved/queued identities, local file bytes,
HTTP statuses, DOM text, error events and resource bounds. Every important changed
path needs a failure-sensitive assertion. No numeric coverage percentage is enforced.
Add isolated `unittest` cases to `test_regressions.py`; temporary directories and mocks
must clean up. The original harness remains a standalone process because it uses
module globals and exits. Independent Node test contexts isolate DOM state. There
are no real sleeps in the regression suites; fixture server shutdown may wait for
its bounded polling interval.

## Limits and empirical eligibility

No held-out evaluation corpus, benchmark score or promotion surface exists. Ordinary
unit/smoke checks are the must-pass gate, not an empirical optimization metric. No
champion is persisted. Real browser installation, private host tool correctness,
Windows no-follow support, large-site performance and live model/embedding integration
are not verified by these fixtures. Dependency metadata auditing may access official
package/advisory services separately from tests.

# Source: docs/INSTALLATION.md

# Installation

## Prerequisites

- macOS or Linux (Windows unverified — see docs/known-issues.md #8)
- Python ≥ 3.11 with pip
- Chrome (only if you want the extension)

## Install

**Option A — zero-install (self-bootstrap).** Just run it; on first start it pip-installs
trafilatura/lxml into the current interpreter if missing:

```bash
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py https://example.org/ --max-depth 1
```

**Option B — venv (recommended for development):**

```bash
python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

**Option C — pre-provision an interpreter:**

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh                      # uses python3
PYTHON=/path/to/python bash scripts/install.sh
```

## Chrome extension

1. `python3 scripts/text_mirror.py --serve` (leaves the API on 127.0.0.1:8765)
2. `chrome://extensions` → enable **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** → select
   `chrome-plugin/`
3. Click the toolbar icon → side panel opens.

## Verify

```bash
python3 -m py_compile scripts/text_mirror.py           # no output = OK
python3 tests/test_text_mirror.py                      # ends with ALL PASS
python3 scripts/text_mirror.py https://example.org/ --max-depth 1
ls text-mirror/                                        # example.org.md + crawl.log
```

## Upgrade

```bash
git pull
pip install -U -r requirements.txt
```

Extension: `chrome://extensions` → reload the unpacked extension.

## Uninstall

Delete the repo clone; remove the unpacked extension in `chrome://extensions`;
`pip uninstall trafilatura lxml` if you installed them globally. Crawl output lives
only under your chosen `--out` locations.


See [Testing](TESTING.md) for all offline gates and [the wiki](wiki/README.md) for the maintained command index.

# Source: docs/integrations-and-assumptions.md

# Integrations and assumptions

## Core runtime

Python 3.11+ runs `scripts/text_mirror.py` and imports `site_clone.py`, trafilatura and
lxml. The CLI fetches operator-selected HTTP(S) URLs; robots uses urllib with a 30s
timeout. Markdown pages append with the exact existing 90-equals / `URL:` / 90-equals
banner. Clone assets use urllib, a 30s timeout, a 32 MiB body cap, and effective redirect
URLs for CSS. Assets may come from other hosts unless same-host-assets is selected.
The local API binds 127.0.0.1:8765. The panel uses localhost:8765 with server CORS.
No third-party backend, database, package build or MCP server is shipped.

## Optional workstation integrations

| Entry | Dependency / default location | Side effects / verification |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh crawl, prefer-llms on | `llms_acquire` from `~/.global-ai-hub/scripts` when present | HTTP acquisition and local Markdown output; read URL headers; bypassed for cloning/sharding/refresh or existing output |
| POST `/crawl_llms_txt` | `claude` CLI and crawl-to-llms-txt skill | Headless editing agent; may use network/models and incur charges; bounded FIFO, 3600s timeout, changed-directory check; no guarantee of semantic correctness |
| POST `/distill` | `~/dev/distillers/distill_offline.py` | Semantic distill subprocess with `--semantic`; 600s timeout; scratch under the installed skill's text-mirror tree |
| Same distill job | `~/.global-ai-hub/.venv/bin/python` and `~/.global-ai-hub/scripts/docset_indexer.py` | Indexes master; 120s timeout; only subprocess exit is checked, independent backend readback is unavailable here |

These are operator-only optional capabilities, not dependencies of the bundled panel.
Tests block host module imports and mock subprocesses. Maintenance does not invoke
these capabilities, activate services or generate semantic embeddings.

## Configuration and boundaries

`CRAWL_DELAY` defaults to 1.0; `MAX_DEPTH` defaults to 0; CLI flags override them.
`PYTHON` selects the explicit installer's interpreter. `.env` is not loaded by Python;
use exported variables (see `.env.example`). Port, worker count, timeouts, API body cap,
queue bounds and optional-tool paths are named module constants. There is no UI for
all operator settings. This small single-file CLI intentionally keeps constants with
their owner rather than adding a settings service.

No authentication is performed against crawled sites. Skip lists are heuristics, not
a proof that content is public. A rendered browser DOM may contain private data; the
operator must select suitable content. URLs can expose sensitive query data in local
logs; avoid credentials, tokens and sensitive URLs. Clone output retains original
active page scripts; open only trusted captured content.

# Source: docs/known-issues.md

# Known issues and maintainer choices

| Surface | Exact limitation / action |
|---|---|
| Legacy state | Host-only state predates destination identity. It is preserved and not reused by the new keyed state. Use a new output destination for a clean post-upgrade crawl; retain the prior corpus. No destructive migration runs automatically. |
| Clone format upgrade | Version2 manifests retain canonical HTML/CSS and cumulative identities. Older/invalid manifests are refused without overwrite; choose a new clone directory. Assets/page source reads are bounded at 32 MiB. |
| HTML clone sharding | Unsupported; construction/CLI rejects it. Text-only sharding remains supported with depth metadata. |
| Cloning failures/caps | Unavailable resources keep live absolute references. A partial clone is not wholly offline; inspect failed/pending manifest entries. |
| Resource limits | Assets are bounded at 32 MiB each; max-assets bounds attempts. BFS/text state still grows with the URL space; set max-depth/max-pages. |
| Dynamic sites | CLI fetches raw HTML. The extension can submit a rendered DOM; dynamically loaded subsequent assets/API interactions are not replayed. |
| Local trust | API has no user authentication. Any local process and allowlisted extension can call it. It is not a multi-user or internet-facing service. |
| Robots | Robots bodies above 512 KiB deny with a log. Existing behavior allows 4xx and transport-unavailable robots, denies 5xx. This is a documented project choice; transport fail-open is not an RFC-compliance guarantee. |
| Optional integrations | Host tools/paths are external and unversioned. Agent route may incur charges; distill route performs semantic indexing. No live integration validation or embedding execution occurred in maintenance. Indexer exit success is not independent backend readback. |
| Dependency bootstrap | First import can pip-install with existing escalation strategies. Preprovision a venv. Runtime floors are updated; full transitive reproducibility is not locked. |
| Browser/OS coverage | Chrome minimum is 116 for sidePanel.open. Node fixture tests do not establish real-browser behavior. POSIX no-follow writes are tested on macOS/Ubuntu; Windows is unsupported by the clone writer. |
| Policy choices | Existing MIT license and code of conduct retained. No new security response SLA, compliance attestation, license or legal promise is supplied. Maintainer must choose any future policy. |
| Workflow integration | Hub registry work is delegated to the batch supervisor. Semantic generation stays paused. Global skill installation, concept-tree mutation and daemon activation are outside this repo task. |

# Source: docs/external-calls.md

# External calls

The generated [operations inventory](operations-registry.json) is owned by
`python scripts/maintain_docs.py`; [route inventory](tool-inventory.json) lists all
8 HTTP routes and zero MCP tools. The registry records source symbols, transport,
targets, triggers, retry/error/remediation policy and actual persistence checks.

| Operation | Logger / test / documentation | Retry and safety |
|---|---|---|
| Page fetch and save | fetch-error/no-content/save-error; smoke + API fixture; Components | No automatic write retry; global request throttle |
| Robots | robots HTTP/unreachable events; synthetic failure fixtures; Architecture | Other scheme on transport failure; documented allow/deny policy |
| Asset fetch | clone-asset-request/ok/error; clone fixtures; Components | Every attempt paced; bounded response; no retry; manifest failure accounting |
| Pip bootstrap + install | bootstrap/installer stdout and failure exit; static command checks; Installation | Existing import-time escalation; explicit venv preferred |
| Optional llms_acquire | acquisition/fallback events; blocked/mock in suites; Integrations | Fallback to text crawl; never called during maintenance |
| Optional agent | start/finish + job history; setup-failure fixture; Integrations | Bounded FIFO/timeouts; billable external capability; no automatic retry |
| Optional distill/index | job status/index outcome; subprocess mocks only; Integrations | Semantic writes; external tools; exit-only backend verification residual |
| Panel API | visible status + console error; VM fixtures; extension runbook | No write retry; status poll; HTTP failures checked |
| Static generator | command output/drift paths; CI --check; Development | Local git read + atomic generated-file replacement; no network/models |

## Five-standard service contract applicability

| Standard | This architecture |
|---|---|
| CLI/MCP operation trigger | Crawler/install/generator have direct CLI commands; browser save/stop and optional jobs use explicit documented local HTTP operations. No general-purpose operations runner is introduced. |
| Central JSONL error service | Inapplicable as a server-platform requirement: core uses local crawl.log/stdout; panel uses visible errors; job history is in memory. No new global error datastore is installed. |
| Remediation map | Inventory provides operation-specific manual remedies. No autonomous remediator is shipped or started. |
| Dashboard cards | Inapplicable: the small panel exposes current crawl stats and controls, not a service dashboard. No dashboard is invented. |
| Datastore readback | Markdown/clone writes have behavioral fixture checks; state/clone/generated references write atomically. Read-only calls have no datastore. Optional external indexer has an explicit independent-readback gap. |

This is architecture-adapted coverage, not a claim that a generic five-standard
service audit passed. File writes and subprocesses have their real side effects
listed. Test fixtures use only temporary synthetic data and mocked optional tools.
